body.p: Claims 1, 5, 10, 14, 18, and 20 are amended. Claims 1-20 remain pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the remarks presented below.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the telephonic interview conducted January 11, 2024. Participating in the interview were Examiner Raymond P. Dulman and Applicant's representative, Arthi Srinivasan (Reg. No. 73,675). During the interview, Applicant'srepresentative discussed the rejection of independent claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 in light of a proposed amendment to claim 1. The Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment would overcome the current rejection but that further search would be needed. Applicant notes similar amendments to those discussed during the interview have been made to the independent claims herein.
No agreement regarding allowability was reached.
Claims 5, 14, and 20 were objected to due to informalities. Applicant has amended these claims to recite "converting the estimated protein value" as requested by the Office.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection be withdrawn.
The Office Action rejected claims 1-3, 5, 7-12, 14, and 16-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as

being unpatentable over Weinert (U.S. Publication No. 20070179434 Al, hereinafter WEINERT) in view of Singley (U.S. Publication No. 20050187749 A1, hereinafter STINGLEY). Claims 4 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over WEINERT in view of SINGLEY as applied to claims 2 and 11, and further in view of Mazlish (U.S. Publication No. 20180200439 Al, hereinafter MAZLISH). Claims 6 and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over WEINERT in view of SINGLEY as applied to claims 5 and 14, and further in view of Moore (U.S. Patent No. 5836312 A, hereinafter MOORE).
Without conceding in the basis of the rejection, and solely to expedite prosecution of this application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 10, and 18 to recite, inter alia,

"converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value by applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the estimated protein value by a patient-specific conversion factor." Support for this amendment can be found in at least paragraph [0080] of the originally filed specification.

In rejecting independent claim 1, prior to the current amendments, the Office correctly acknowledged that Weinert does not disclose or suggest "converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value by applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the estimated protein value by a carbohydrate value." However, the Office asserted that Singley discloses this feature. (Office Action, page 5).

Singley states that "the grams of carbs from proteins can be calculated by taking the food weight of the food being weighed by the scale and multiplying it by a multiplier appropriate for the weight units being used to weigh the food. For example, it is known that 1 ounce of a 'protein food' (e.g., meat, poultry, etc.) equals 4.2 grams of carbs from protein. Thus, if we have

3 ounces of chicken, we can calculate that we have 12.6 grams carbs from that protein." (Singley, paragraph [0025]). In other words, Singley describes using a fixed carbs from protein value for a given food. Nowhere does Singley disclose or suggest using a patient-specific conversion factor to "convert the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value."

Moreover, Applicant notes that during the telephonic interview, the Examiner agreed the amendment to independent claims 1, 10, and 18 would overcome the current rejection over Weinert in view of Singley.

Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable. Moreover, Applicant respectfully submits that dependent claims 2-9, 11-17, 19, and 20, each of which depend from one of independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable for at least the same reasons independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable.
Applicant respectfully submits dependent claims 6 and 15, which recite "wherein the
conversion factor is determined based on historical meal data for the patient and further based on
historical glucose level data for the patient" are allowable for at least a second reason.

In rejecting dependent claims 6 and 15, the Office conceded that Weinert and Singley fail to disclose or suggest that the conversion factor is determined based on historical meal data and historical glucose level data, but asserted that Moore discloses this feature. (Office Action, page 21).
The cited portion of Moore describes "determining whether [an] information string

relates to a consumed item or measured physiological parameter," which is "stored along with time data coupled thereto in a subdirectory directed to the physiological measurement." In other words, the cited portion of Moore merely describes techniques for generating a log of items consumed and physiological data, and makes no mention of "a conversion factor," let alone one used to "convert [an] estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value." The cited portion of Moore is entirely unrelated to converting an estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value, and accordingly cannot and does not disclose or suggest that a conversion factor for performing such a conversion is "determined based on historical meal data for the patient and further based on historical glucose level data for the patient."
Applicant respectfully submits that dependent claims 7 and 16, which recite "the
conversion factor is determined based on a time of day that the user consumes the meal," are allowable for at least a second reason.
In rejecting dependent claims 7 and 16, the Office asserted that Singley discloses this

feature. Singley states "[t]he tool can record the event with the following pieces of information: Time of meal, Foods and weights, Meal bolus computation, BG reading, time of BG reading (pre meal), meal type (Breakfast, lunch, dinner), HBG adjustment, & LBG adjustment (if any)." (Singley, paragraph [0061], cited by the Office).
Applicant respectfully submits that Singley merely states that time of day can be
recorded, and makes no mention of a conversion factor being determined based on the time of day, as recited in dependent claims 7 and 16.
For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

The remarks presented herein are fully responsive to the Office Action and are sufficient to overcome the rejections presented in the Office Action. Applicant requests withdrawal of the instant rejections and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. Should any issues remain outstanding, the Examiner is urged to telephone the undersigned to expedite prosecution.
Respectfully Submitted,
